missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Песня' stays in the nominative as the subject. 'Любимая' is the agreeing feminine adjective and 'моя' the possessive. A clean descriptive model.
Strategic focus: Accusative direct object. 'Песню' is the accusative object of 'поёт'; feminine nouns in '-я' take '-ю'. 'Красивую' agrees in the feminine accusative.
Strategic focus: Genitive after negation. 'Песни' is the genitive after the negated 'не знаю'. 'Этой' is the agreeing feminine genitive form. A natural way to admit you don't know something.
Strategic focus: Dative with 'к'. 'Песне' is the dative after 'к', marking what the music belongs to. 'Музыку' is the accusative object that was written. A natural creative-work frame.
Strategic focus: Accusative with 'под'. 'Песню' is the accusative after 'под' to mean dancing to a song. 'Эту' agrees in the feminine accusative. A common everyday phrase.
Strategic focus: Instrumental case. 'Песней' is the instrumental governed by 'наслаждаться'. 'Этой' agrees in the feminine instrumental. A natural verb that demands this case.
Strategic focus: Prepositional case. 'В песне' uses the prepositional 'песне' after 'в' to locate meaning within the song. 'Этой' is the agreeing feminine prepositional form.
Strategic focus: Nominative plural subject. 'Песни' is the nominative plural, the subject of 'звучат'. 'Эти' is the agreeing plural form. Good for the feminine plural ending '-и'.
Strategic focus: Genitive plural with a fleeting vowel. 'Песен' is the genitive plural after 'много'; a fleeting 'е' appears between the consonants. 'Русских' agrees in the plural genitive.
Strategic focus: Accusative direct object. 'Песню' is the accusative object of 'послушаем'. 'Новую' agrees in the feminine accusative, and 'давай' makes a friendly suggestion.
